validity_note: True: step-up covers only EMAIL_CHANGE and PASSWORD_CHANGE, and no billing endpoint checks a token. Caveats: billing endpoints exist only when app.payments.enabled=true (OFF today); payment methods and portal cancellation live in the Stripe-hosted portal, so the in-app action is POST /subscription/portal; invoice data means registry CompanyData.

must_find.why: proves CompanyData is the invoice buyer data

must_find.why: where the FE issues consent + upgrade writes

key_facts.claim: There are two actions (EMAIL_CHANGE, PASSWORD_CHANGE) and two challenges (EMAIL_CODE, TOTP). checkRequirement gives 403 for PENDING_ADMIN, TOTP for ADMIN, required=false for COMPANY or INFLUENCER without initialAccountSetupCompleted, and EMAIL_CODE otherwise. TOTP setup is admin-only.

The email code is 6 digits, stored as a SHA-256 hash in Redis for 10 minutes and sent to lastVerifiedEmail. After 5 wrong codes: 15-minute cooldown (429). After 3 cycles in 24 hours: 24-hour lockout (423). The email does not say which action the code is for.

verify issues a UUID token stored at hash(uid):ACTION for 10 minutes. validateAndConsumeToken does an atomic getAndDelete and compares it with the X-Step-Up-Token header; a mismatch returns 401. Tokens are single-use and per action but not bound to the request payload.
The endpoints are GET /step-up/check, POST /step-up/request and POST /step-up/verify, all isAuthenticated with the STRICT rate limit. verify uses TOTP for ADMIN and the email code for everyone else.

Enforcement is written out by hand in each controller; there is no filter or annotation. PATCH/PUT /users/{id} checks EMAIL_CHANGE only when the email actually changes, and /auth/firebase/change-password checks PASSWORD_CHANGE.

validateTokenIfRequired skips when step-up is not required. A COMPANY becomes ACTIVE (COMPANY authority) with a verified email and company data alone, but setup completion also needs a full profile. Reused for billing, it lets active companies with incomplete profiles skip step-up.

SubscriptionPaidController exposes /trial/activate, /consent, /upgrade, /downgrade, /downgrade/cancel and /portal without step-up. Upgrading an existing subscriber charges the proration at once (ALWAYS_INVOICE), a trial downgrade to FREE is immediate, and /portal returns a Stripe-hosted session.

Invoice buyer data is CompanyData (name, NIP, GUS address), which InvoiceRetryService reads for every invoice. It is written by POST /registry/confirm, POST /registry/refresh and DELETE /registry/company-data.

On the FE, the STEP_UP_TOKEN context, the interceptor and StepUpDialogComponent are used only by EmailChangeComponent. The billing client methods accept no HttpContext, and the FE StepUpActionType is generated from OpenAPI, so a new action needs a BE enum change, regeneration and new client signatures.

The existing proof is Cucumber step-up-auth.feature (happy path, 401 without a token, reuse 401, cooldown, 403, TOTP), ported to the FE as step-up-email-required.spec.ts. No backend unit or integration test targets StepUpAuthService.

gaps.finding: No billing write in SubscriptionPaidController has step-up or @RateLimit. That includes the one-POST proration charge and cancelDowngrade, which turns renewal back on.

Soft account deletion (DELETE /users/{id} -> archiveUser -> deactivateForAccountDeletion) cancels the Stripe subscription immediately with only isAuthenticated, and the FE dialog admits it has no step-up.

DELETE /registry/company-data deletes a paying company's CompanyData and leaves its status unchanged (the OpenAPI text wrongly says it reverts to IN_VALIDATION). Later invoices fail with No company data found and end up in DEAD_LETTER.
POST /auth/firebase/update-email changes the email through EmailChangeService with only a password check. It bypasses the EMAIL_CHANGE step-up that /users/{id} enforces.
The FE never gets a PASSWORD_CHANGE token. SecuritySettingsComponent calls changePassword without one, so users with completed setup get a 401 that the page shows as a wrong current password.
A null dialog result means either cancelled or not required, and EmailChangeComponent treats every null as cancel. Billing flows that reuse the dialog must tell the two apart.

invariants: Tokens stay single-use, short-lived and per action: an EMAIL_CHANGE or PASSWORD_CHANGE token never authorizes billing, and the reverse holds too.
A missing or invalid token gets a 401 before any Stripe call, consent record, customer creation or DB write; enforcement lives on the server.
Billing step-up applies to every active COMPANY regardless of initialAccountSetupCompleted; existing email and password semantics are unchanged.
Stripe webhooks, crons and system flows stay token-free.
Codes go only to lastVerifiedEmail, cooldown and lockout stay per action, and the /step-up API changes only by adding enum values.
good_designs: Add billing action types (plan change, portal, invoice data, account deletion) and check them at the service layer with an always-required validateAndConsumeToken, ideally bound to the target plan; on the FE, open StepUpDialog before each billing write and pass withStepUpToken through the updated frozen clients.

Build a reusable @RequiresStepUp(action) aspect that reads X-Step-Up-Token, apply it to SubscriptionPaidController, the registry writes and user deletion, then move EMAIL_CHANGE and PASSWORD_CHANGE onto it and close the update-email bypass.

Order and proof: enum and policy with StepUpAuthService unit tests (always required, action isolation, single use); Cucumber per endpoint (401 without token, 200 with, reuse 401, no Stripe call on 401, webhooks unaffected); regenerate OpenAPI; update FE clients and dialogs with Jest and Playwright ports.
red_flags: Reuse validateTokenIfRequired as-is: active companies with incomplete profiles would skip billing step-up.
An email-change token or a fresh login already covers billing: tokens are per action and consumed once.
Step-up runs in a Spring Security filter or annotation: it is explicit calls in two controllers.
Offer TOTP to companies, or protect payment-method endpoints in the app: TOTP is admin-only, and payment methods change in the Stripe-hosted portal.
Require step-up on /webhooks/stripe or the crons, or expect the generated client to send the header to /subscription/*: that client is hand-written.

architecture.today: StepUpActionType (EMAIL_CHANGE, PASSWORD_CHANGE) scopes all Redis keys; checkRequirement gives ADMIN TOTP, PENDING_ADMIN 403, setup-incomplete users none, others EMAIL_CODE.
architecture.fit: Adds billing actions with an always-required check, reusing the email code, cooldown and lockout.
architecture.breaks: A billing PIN or OTP, TOTP for companies, reusing EMAIL_CHANGE, or validateTokenIfRequired as-is.

architecture.today: /step-up/check, /request and /verify (STRICT rate limit) yield a 10-minute token per user and action; validateAndConsumeToken getAndDeletes it, compares X-Step-Up-Token (CORS-allowed) and throws a 401 translatable exception on mismatch.
architecture.fit: Billing writes consume a token for their own action from that header before any Stripe call or DB write.
architecture.breaks: A JWT claim or recently-verified flag, a new header or error shape, or reusable tokens.

architecture.today: UserController and FirebaseAuthProxyController call stepUpAuthService explicitly; @RequiresRecaptcha with RecaptchaValidationAspect already checks a header token by annotation.
architecture.fit: Calls the service in billing, registry and user-deletion endpoints, or adds @RequiresStepUp on the reCAPTCHA aspect pattern.
architecture.breaks: Frontend-only enforcement, or a validator or filter bypassing validateAndConsumeToken.

architecture.today: Billing writes exist only when app.payments.enabled, are COMPANY-only and @Hidden from OpenAPI; payment methods change in the Stripe portal; webhooks use Stripe-Signature.
architecture.fit: Adds step-up inside the gated controller or its service calls; webhooks and crons stay token-free.
architecture.breaks: Step-up on webhooks or crons, endpoints outside the gate, or in-app payment-method endpoints.

architecture.pattern: Frontend token context, interceptor and dialog
architecture.today: StepUpDialogComponent returns a token or null (cancel or not required); UserApiService passes withStepUpToken as HttpContext and stepUpInterceptor sets the header; the hand-written billing client takes no context.
architecture.fit: Opens the dialog per billing action, threads an optional token through SubscriptionWriteApi, the frozen client and registry wrapper, and regenerates StepUpActionType.
architecture.breaks: Headers set in components, a second dialog or interceptor, HttpClient in feature code, or edits under src/app/api.

architecture.today: A tag-run Cucumber feature proves step-up (happy path, missing or reused token 401, cooldown, 403); a Playwright integration spec ports and cites it.
architecture.fit: Adds billing scenarios there (401 before Stripe, action isolation, webhooks untouched) and ports them.
architecture.breaks: Only mocked unit tests, or FE specs without a BE scenario.
